rationale: B responds coherently to all salient inputs (touch, call, food offer, present-ball, startle) and also initiates sensible shifts among play objects and people (mirror→person on call, person→chime, chime→food, later back to cube and person). Its attention patterns persist and evolve, including a prolonged, graded response to the aversive buzzer. A shows narrower focus (mainly the ball, later 'none'), fails to adjust to the call and presented ball, and quickly reverts after startle. Overall, B exhibits richer, more autonomous and adaptive behavior over time.
